newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eurotunnel investors face massive dilution.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel investors face massive dilution.

text.p: Shareholders in Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel SA /Plc could see their holding in the capital reduced to 39.4 percent if the company's creditor banks exercise all their equity notes, or convertible bonds.

French co-chairman Patrick Ponsolle told a news conference on Monday that shareholders would hold 54.5 percent of the capital after an initial debt-for-equity swap retired eight billion francs of junior-ranked loans.
But if banks exercise their conversion rights on equity notes, used to take out a further eight billion of debt, shareholders' share could fall to 39.4 percent of the capital.

To avoid that further dilution, Eurotunnel will give one free share warrant for every three shares held to current shareholders allowing them to buy one new share at 12 francs between now and the end of 2003.
If all these warrants are exercised, shareholders would hold 51.3 percent of the capital, Ponsolle said.
The proceeds of the take-up of share warrants would go towards repaying the equity notes, exercisable in 2003.
The company's future should be clearer around 2003, when the restructuring period ends, he said.

Shareholders will also be able to subscribe to new shares on favourable terms when the debt-for-equity swap is done with the banks. The principle has been agreed with the 24 instructing banks but the precise terms have yet to be fixed.
